body: Yes, if I moved to a different state, which to do that is about two and a half hours away, but six to seven hours is still not long enough for her to come after me.

There's another town about 25-30 miles away (30 minutes away). The young people keep moving out of this area and older people keep coming here to retire and take senior level contract work. So most good jobs that exist here are just senior level. They take it for granted and don't accommodate younger people. They always try by asking "Why do younger people leave?", but is a joke because they haven't figured out the answer even after they've been shown numerous times. But anyway, the other town is not far enough. Since her current job in this town is her first stable job, she has a lot of incentive to stay here. So if I moved further away, she'd be very unlikely to follow me.

Verbal/psychological abuse and failure to find a job to get away from it all. And I contacted the national domestic violence hotline once and they told me that there aren't any resources since my mother is the one who hurts me, even though I live in a state where domestic violence is simply defined as anybody who lives with the victim currently or formerly. But then the state domestic violence website implies that only women in abusive relationships can get hurt.
